memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Benign positional vertigo with episodic positional dizziness.
Patient reports brief spinning sensations on lying down or turning head, lasting <1 minute, associated nausea. No hearing loss or tinnitus. Dix-Hallpike test positive on right side with torsional nystagmus. Audiometry shows bilateral mild high‑frequency sensorineural loss. She is a non‑smoker, never smoked. Inhaler not prescribed. Technique not applicable.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
betahistine 16 mg twice daily
meclizine 25 mg as needed for vertigo
salbutamol metered‑dose inhaler 2 puffs as needed for wheeze

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Audiometry: Right ear 25 dB HL at 4 kHz, 30 dB at 6 kHz; Left ear 20 dB HL at 4 kHz, 25 dB at 6 kHz. Speech discrimination 96% bilaterally. Consistent with mild high‑frequency sensorineural loss.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Dix‑Hallpike test: Right side positive, torsional up‑beating nystagmus lasting 8 seconds. Left side negative.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked for 2025‑07‑10 at 10:00 AM with Dr Suresh Menon (D05).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Benign positional vertigo, improved; occasional mild wheeze.
Vertigo episodes reduced to 1‑2 per week, shorter duration. Patient uses meclizine only occasionally. Reports occasional chest tightness on exertion, relieved by salbutamol. Spirometry shows FEV1 2.85 L (92% predicted), FVC 3.40 L (95%), FEV1/FVC 0.84, unchanged from baseline. Asthma Control Test score 22 (well controlled). Inhaler technique checked: correct. Smoking status: never smoked.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
betahistine 24 mg twice daily
meclizine 25 mg as needed
salbutamol metered‑dose inhaler 2 puffs as needed

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Repeat audiometry: Right ear 22 dB HL at 4 kHz, 28 dB at 6 kHz; Left ear 18 dB HL at 4 kHz, 22 dB at 6 kHz. Stable mild high‑frequency loss.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Spirometry: FEV1 2.85 L (92% pred), FVC 3.40 L (95% pred), FEV1/FVC 0.84. Change in FEV1 since last test: +0.02 L.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Feeling much better; vertigo rare now. Only occasional mild wheeze when I climb stairs, which improves with my inhaler. No side effects from betahistine.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Benign positional vertigo, well controlled; asthma mild intermittent.
Vertigo free for past 6 weeks. No need for meclizine. Asthma symptoms absent, salbutamol used <2 times/week. Spirometry: FEV1 2.92 L (94% pred), FVC 3.45 L (96% pred), FEV1/FVC 0.85, +0.07 L increase since last visit. Asthma Control Test 24 (well controlled). Inhaler technique correct. Smoking status: never smoked.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
betahistine stopped
meclizine 25 mg as needed only
salbutamol metered‑dose inhaler 2 puffs as needed

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Audiometry: Right ear 20 dB HL at 4 kHz, 26 dB at 6 kHz; Left ear 16 dB HL at 4 kHz, 20 dB at 6 kHz. No significant change from baseline.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Spirometry: FEV1 2.92 L (94% pred), FVC 3.45 L (96% pred), FEV1/FVC 0.85. Change in FEV1 since last test: +0.07 L.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Next review appointment booked for 2026‑02‑14 at 09:30 AM with Dr Suresh Menon (D05).

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Referral to ENT specialist for vestibular rehabilitation assessment. Patient has resolved positional vertigo; request advice on vestibular therapy and any further work‑up for persistent mild high‑frequency hearing loss.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: ENT report: Benign positional vertigo confirmed, no central pathology. Audiology shows stable mild high‑frequency sensorineural loss, likely age‑related. Recommended vestibular rehabilitation exercises twice daily for 6 weeks; no further intervention needed.
